“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” Israel’s gates shall be open continually, “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” And “the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” Strangers left alive to serve Israel, as the Gibeonites were, is future prophecy as well as history.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

precepts.why:
The princes were deceived, yet when all the congregation murmured they held the line: “We have sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.” “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”. The princes could have said the oath was an error, but they did not; what comes out of your mouth, be sure to do it, lest God be angry at thy voice and destroy the work of thine hands. Our forefathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding up to their word.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

precepts.why:
“let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation”. Hewers of wood and drawers of water means slaves. This is according to the law of the Most High pertaining to other nations: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you”, and of “the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you”; “they shall be your bondmen for ever”, an inheritance for your children after you. The Gibeonites were heathen dwelling among Israel, so the oath to let them live did not set them free; it set them to serve.

If you just read the Old Testament, there was no equality among the nations, and there is still no equality among nations: they were made for a certain purpose. The one line drawn is among ourselves: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” The reason the nations are not in their purpose now is because we have sinned and failed, and one day Israel will rise again to put them back in their rightful places.
